data.name: Manarat
data.gender_notes: Manarat is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Manarat refers to beacons or guides. This name is derived from the Arabic word 'manara', which means a guiding light or a beacon. This name is often given to girls whose parents wish them to become beacons of light and knowledge for others. The name Manarat carries the meaning “Guides, Beacons” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic. Parents who choose Manarat usually hope their child will grow to embody guides, beacons and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of guidance and enlightenment, representing the path to knowledge and wisdom.
data.etymology: Manarat belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guides, Beacons.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Manarat total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
